smoking.title: Heart rate and blood pressure start to come down
smoking.detail: Soon after your last cigarette, your heart rate and blood pressure begin to settle.

smoking.title: Carbon monoxide in your blood drops to normal
smoking.detail: Carbon monoxide from smoke takes the place of oxygen in your blood. Within a few days it falls back to normal.

smoking.title: Circulation and lung function improve
smoking.detail: Somewhere in this window, blood flow and breathing start to work better.

smoking.title: Coughing and shortness of breath ease
smoking.detail: The tiny hairs that clear your lungs start working again, so coughing and breathlessness ease.

smoking.title: Heart attack risk drops sharply
smoking.detail: One to two years after quitting, the risk of a heart attack drops sharply.

smoking.title: Risk of mouth, throat and voice-box cancer is about halved
smoking.detail: Five to ten years after quitting, the risk of these cancers is cut by about half, and the risk of stroke goes down.

smoking.title: Lung cancer risk is about half that of someone who still smokes
smoking.detail: Ten years after quitting, the risk of dying from lung cancer is about half that of a person who still smokes.

smoking.title: Heart disease risk is close to that of a non-smoker
smoking.detail: Fifteen years after quitting, the risk of coronary heart disease is close to that of someone who never smoked.

nicotine.title: Withdrawal can start
nicotine.line: Cravings, restlessness or irritability are common.
nicotine.detail: Withdrawal can begin within a few hours of your last nicotine. It's a sign your body is adjusting.

nicotine.title: Most nicotine has left your body
nicotine.line: Its by-product, cotinine, halves about every 15 to 20 hours.
nicotine.detail: Nicotine itself clears within hours. Cotinine, what your body turns it into, halves about every 15 to 20 hours, so within a few days most of it is gone.

nicotine.title: Withdrawal is usually at its strongest
nicotine.line: The hardest stretch for most people.
nicotine.detail: For most people, withdrawal is strongest in the first days to week, then weakens the longer you stay nicotine-free.

nicotine.title: Mood changes from withdrawal usually ease
nicotine.detail: Low mood, irritability or anxiety from withdrawal usually get better within a week or two. If they don't, talk to a doctor.

nicotine.title: Cravings come less often
nicotine.detail: Cravings can last longer than the physical symptoms, but they come less often and feel weaker as the weeks go by.

vape.note: Research on the long-term effects of vaping is still young, so this timeline sticks to what's known.

pouches.note: Research on the long-term effects of nicotine pouches is still young, so this timeline sticks to what's known.
